messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Passing Global variable in map expression
parts:
There are several ways.

1. For a large number of variables (or large in size e.g. a few MB)

rhsave(n1,n2,n3, file="/path-on-hdfs/data.Rdata")

map.setup = expression({
load("data.Rdata") # no need to give full path
})


rhmr(...,setup=list(map=map.setup),
shared.files=c("/path-on-hdfs/data.Rdata"),....


2. Serialize as strings and pass via mapred

mapred=list()
mapred$c1 = rawToChar(serialize(c1,NULL,ascii=TRUE))
mapred$c2 = rawToChar(serialize(c2,NULL,ascii=TRUE))


map.setup = expression({
c1 = unserialize( charToRaw( Sys.getenv("c1") ))
c2 = unserialize( charToRaw( Sys.getenv("c2") ))
})

rhmr(,.., mapred=mapred,setup=list(map=map.setup))


3. Modify R code using bquote (you should be comfortable with
modifying code at run time)


map = as.expression(bquote({
c1 <- .(c1)
c2 <- .(c2)
.....}, list(c1=c1,c2=c2)))

rhmr(map=map,...)

Note, this code is parsed and modified before being sent to Hadoop. c1
and c2 are hardcoded into the source. Try this

c1=matrix(runif(10),ncol=2)
c2=matrix(runif(10),ncol=2)
map = as.expression(bquote({
c1 <- .(c1)
c2 <- .(c2)
}, list(c1=c1,c2=c2)))

and type map, you'll see c1 and c2 in the source. Use this for i)
small number of global variables ii) small sized variables (< MB)


Regards

Saptarshi

messages.subject: Re: Passing Global variable in map expression
parts:
Hi,
I figured out by writing so many map reduce jobs that error in readbin
is thrown for the following
reasons:
1. Input and output folder are wrongly mentioned
For example: if the original input file created is "input/file"
and in the code you have provided as ifolder="/input/file".

In this case readBin error is thrown.

2. If you are storing the data on HDFS using the function rhsave like
rhsave(x,y,file="data/dat.Rdata")
and in the map set up expression you are calling as load("dat.RData")
{Note the diff Rdata and RData "D" is caps), in this case error is
thrown

If you do vice versa also i.e. storing the file on HDFS as
rhsave(x,"data/dat.RData") and accessing in the map set up expression
as load("dat.Rdata") then also error is thrown

3. If you are trying to access the matrix or data frame with incorrect
index then also error is thrown

Well in most of the cases this error is thrown if there is some
logical problem in the code only.
I guess there are other cases aswell where this error is thrown, i
think you can update me more on this kind of error.

Well cant these error be made more specific to the problem?

Regards,
Shekhar

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Re: Passing Global variable in map expression
parts:
I've said this before.

1. If you use rhex(z) and call the script using source, you wont see
errors. The error code is because there
were hadoop/R errors. The errors are printed out by hadoop and using
source will hide these. If you use rhex(z)
then either
a) run rhex(z) interactively at the prompt
b) if you call it via source, then go to the jobtracker and look for the errors

2. You can also try this (either using source or interactively)

j <- rhex(z, async=TRUE)
jr <- rhstatus(j, mon.sec=5,autokill=TRUE)

the last line monitors the job and will kill it if there are R errors
(but will /not/ kill it if there are Hadoop errors, since Hadoop
errors need not be fatal)
Also, it has attributes that contain the R / Hadoop errors.

parts:
Hmm distilling it down to a minimum test case revealed that it
worked. I changed it to pass environments instead of list and
attached that environment in the setup prior to map/reduce. Seems to
work. Gives an output of 5.0 for each time the mapper was invoked.


rhmrWithEnvSetup = function(env.setup, ...){

mc = match.call()
mc = as.list(mc)
if(!is.null(mc$setup)){
cat("Error: env setup currently incompatable with setup argument.

\n")
}

mc[[1]] = NULL # removes call from list

mc$env.setup = NULL #removes from list
env.setup = rawToChar(serialize(env.setup,NULL,ascii=TRUE))
print(env.setup)
if(!is.null(mc$mapred)){
mc$mapred$env.setup = env.setup
}else{
mc$mapred = list()
mc$mapred$env.setup = env.setup
}
setup = expression({
env.setup = unserialize( charToRaw( Sys.getenv("env.setup") ))
attach(env.setup)
print(ls())

})
mc$setup = setup
return(do.call("rhmr", mc))


}

mapper = expression({
rhcollect(1,test.function())
})


env.setup = new.env()
env.setup$test.function = function(){
return(5)
}
DIR = getwd()
args = list()
args$map = mapper
args$env.setup = env.setup
args$ifolder = paste(DIR,"input",sep="/")
args$ofolder = paste(DIR,"output", sep="/")
args$inout = c("text","text")
args$mapred = list(mapred.job.tracker='local')
mr = do.call("rhmrWithEnvSetup", args)
rhex(mr)
